title: Tito Puente demands top billing over Machito
summary: Puente's hit year of 1952 won him top billing even at the Malibu; Machito accepted for his family and compares himself to Joe Louis.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Okay. Tito Puente was really hot, his best year was 1952 ahh they recorded him 36, 37 times, 72 sides, something like that and because of that he got all that exposure and new tunes. That has to influence the dances at the Palladium ballroom. After that he demanded top billing over everyone. You were the top band at the time, Noro Morales was second, Marcelino Guerra was third. Tito Puente came out of nowhere and demanded top billing over all of them and got it. He even demanded top billing over you at the Malibu. Do you remember that time he demanded that?
Okay, how did you feel about that?
Well, ahh, you just can't fight with the owner of the place and you just can't fight the necessity of work. I had a family and I am very positive that he with all his

talents, and he played very good, but I know what I have. I know that I create what he was playing and that I was playing as best as anybody, so that doesn't bother me. It's like Joe Louis used to say: "Well, he can run, but he can't hide".
Uh- huh. Okay, I get the impression from your answer then that top billing meant nothing to you then.
Does it mean anything to you today?

No, I want to be in the same ring no matter if he is on top or whatever. I want to fight the guy like Joe Louis used to say: "I don't care if he just runs this way and the other way, when he stops I am going to get him."
